A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SageAttention2. The complete 20-page v4 and 22-page v5, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. Relocated and renumbered content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v4 reports original kernel throughput, attention accuracy, generation latency, and model evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains those empirical results and adds quantization-granularity throughput measurements and Qwen2-Audio evaluation results in Tables 19–20.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the per-thread quantization equations are unchanged. Both INT4 and INT8 kernels already appear in v4 Table 3. v5 newly specifies that the existing INT8 variant omits Q smoothing; this disclosure does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v5 adds a limited extension to speech recognition: Qwen2-Audio (7B) evaluated on LibriSpeech in Appendix A.9 and Table 20. The existing language, image, video, image-classification, and long-context coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained experiments preserve their comparator sets. The new audio evaluation reuses Full-Precision, HadmdAttn, SmoothAttn, and SageAttention as baselines; newly cited attention methods are not added as evaluated competitors.

E3.justification: v5 introduces an ASR evaluation using WER, with Table 20 columns labeled Test-Clean and Test-Dev, and a controlled L20 throughput comparison across quantization granularities. Existing protocols are not substantively revised; Appendix A.8 documents previously unstated benchmark settings.

E4.justification: New Table 19 directly tests the throughput cost of per-tensor, per-block, per-thread, and per-token quantization. This complements the retained granularity-accuracy analyses in Tables 6 and 15 and component-overhead analysis in Table 18. Existing visual comparisons are relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v5's Gaussian input standard deviation describes benchmark input generation, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing numerical values in Tables 1–18 and matched kernel plots are retained. New Table 19 reports 283 TOPS for per-thread versus 268 for per-token quantization. Table 20 adds Test-Clean/Test-Dev WER of 1.74/4.01 for Full-Precision, 1.73/3.99 for SageAttn2-4b, and 1.72/4.03 for SageAttn2-8b.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.5 introduces independent Gaussian activation assumptions and derives post-centering means, variances, and probability claims connecting smoothing to quantization error. This adds a substantial formal argument absent from v4. However, Equations (6)–(7) inconsistently substitute upper-tail events into a lower-tail argument and are invalid as printed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three principal contributions and acceleration/accuracy claims. Explicitly identifying SageAttn2-8b for Hopper clarifies which previously evaluated variant supplies the retained result.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly explains Hopper's lack of native INT4 support and extends its applicability discussion to audio. The new claim of consistent superiority on audio overstates Table 20: SageAttn2-8b has Test-Dev WER 4.03, versus 4.01 for SmoothAttn and 4.02 for SageAttention.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.8 specifies batch size 4, 32 attention heads, Gaussian floating-point inputs, and uniformly sampled integer inputs. Section 4.1 also discloses that the existing INT8 variant excludes Q smoothing. These additions improve implementation and benchmark documentation; code access is unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 expands citations to recent attention work, including SageAttention3, SageAttention2++, SpargeAttn, and Sparse VideoGen, and adds references supporting the Gaussian analysis and audio evaluation. The principal positioning as hardware-efficient quantized attention remains stable.

P1.justification: v5 makes local prose and cross-reference corrections, expands several explanations, updates affiliations and publication information, and adds acknowledgment and impact statements. Two appendix subsections are inserted, while the main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reformatted and Figure 4 is redrawn. Existing figures are rearranged, including moving video examples into the main text and splitting v4 Figure 8 into v5 Figures 7 and 9. Tables 19–20 are added, with associated figure and table reflow.

improvement.justification: v5 improves reproducibility through Appendix A.8 and clearer Hopper implementation details, while Table 19 supplies direct evidence for the granularity/throughput tradeoff. However, the new smoothing argument contains invalid probability steps in Equations (6)–(7), and the audio discussion overstates Table 20's mixed results. These documentation and empirical gains coexist with new mathematical and interpretive defects, leaving the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
